item.text:
I did not score 8B.

Shehbaz Sharif’s 2022 program is fairly explicit in the record: stabilize the economy, restart and keep the IMF program, impose difficult fiscal adjustments, protect lower-income households, and respond to the flood emergency with coordinated relief and reconstruction.

**Search and rejection summary**
- I reviewed roughly 30 documents across Reuters wires and Reuters reprints, Ministry of Finance budget materials, IMF press releases and country reports, SBP documentation, PID/BISP releases, and World Bank/WHO flood and macroeconomic assessments.
- I kept the strongest non-duplicative material from the coalition-cabinet / IMF / budget / flood-response / inflation / reconstruction / appointment / financing threads.
- I rejected or downgraded several items as duplicates because they repeated the same Reuters wire on another outlet, especially Euronews, Investing.com, The Business Standard, and other syndication mirrors.
- I treated some health-crisis and flood-emergency pages as context-only when they described the disaster scale but not Sharif’s own execution choices.
- I excluded out-of-period material surfaced during search, including 2024 and 2026 pages, because they were not usable as target-period evidence.
- I avoided padding with generic country-level macro data when it did not add ruler-specific attribution.

**Remaining gaps**
- There is still limited direct evidence on day-to-day command performance inside ministries and how well implementation followed through beyond the announced measures.
- The record is stronger on declared program, fiscal tightening, and emergency response than on independently measured end-of-2022 success.
- More search would help if you want sharper evidence on whether the tax, subsidy, and IMF measures were actually implemented on schedule and whether they changed receipts, deficits, or reserves before year-end.
- The biggest attribution gap is separating Sharif’s own management from inherited fiscal collapse, flood shock, coalition constraints, and IMF conditionality.
